solutionSql:
SELECT customer_id, id
FROM (
  SELECT s.customer_id,
         s.id,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.customer_id ORDER BY s.booked_at DESC, s.id DESC) AS rn
  FROM shipments s
) ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY customer_id;

rules.howSolved: ROW_NUMBER ordered by booked_at descending gives rank 1 to the latest booking.
The query starts from shipments, so customers without shipments never appear.

ambiguities: The instruction does not say how to break a tie on booked_at. In the ties and boundary datasets, one customer has two shipments with the same latest booked_at. I broke the tie with the higher id. A lower-id tie-break changes exactly one returned row in each of those datasets. The sample has no such tie.
notes: Sample returns 6 rows. Tie-break probe: ties and boundary each differ by one row between the higher-id and lower-id choices.
